newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia average wages rise 4.8 pct in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Australia average wages rise 4.8 pct in Q3.

text.p: Australian average annualised wages based on wage agreements covering almost 200,000 employees rose 4.8 percent in the September quarter, down from a revised 5.3 percent in the previous quarter, the Industrial Relations Department said on Thursday.
It said private sector wages rose an average of 5.3 percent in the September quarter, down from a revised 6.1 percent previously.

The department said that at least 1,061 enterprise bargaining agreements, covering an estimated 198,000 employees, were formalised by the Industrial Relations Commission in the quarter. "The pace of federal enterprise bargaining continued to be strong in the September quarter," the department said.
Enterprise bargaining agreements are negotiated on an individual employer basis rather than on an industry-wide scale.
In the private sector, at least 821 agreements, covering about 105,000 employees, were formalised in the quarter.
"However, estimates for both the June and September quarters were heavily influenced by four major bank agreements, which paid above-average wage increases," the department said.
Public sector wages increased an average of 4.0 percent in the September quarter, down from 4.2 percent in the previous quarter.
The June quarter rise for all employees was originally reported at 5.6 percent before revision to 5.3 percent.
The original figure for private sector agreements for the June quarter was 6.6 percent before revision to 6.1 percent.
